en: The *Sūtra on the Ten Powers Spoken by the Buddha*,
translated and presented for imperial inspection by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Muditaśīla at Lianhua Monastery in Anxi.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:

“You should know that all Buddhas, Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas are fully endowed with the ten powers; because they possess these ten powers, they are named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. They are supremely eminent, extraordinary, heroic, and sovereign, capable of turning the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-wheel and uttering the true lion’s roar amidst the great assembly.”
What are these ten? They are as follows:
the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, knows as it truly is what is possible as possible, and knows as it truly is what is impossible as impossible; he knows all things as they truly are.

If the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, in this regard, know as it truly is what is possible as possible, and know as it truly is what is impossible as impossible—because they know possibility and impossibility as they truly are—this is called the first power of knowledge regarding possibility and impossibility.

Possessing this power, he is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; supreme, extraordinary, heroic, and sovereign, he is able to turn the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-wheel and let out the true lion’s roar amidst the great assembly.

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, knows as they truly are all the past, future, and present karmas of sentient beings, as well as the mutual contact of phenomena and their corresponding maturations."

If the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, know as they truly are the past, future, and present karmas of all sentient beings, as well as the mutual contact of phenomena and their corresponding maturations, this is called the second power: the knowledge of the maturation of karma.

Possessing this power, he is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; supreme, preeminent, heroic, and sovereign, he is able to turn the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-wheel and roar the true lion’s roar amidst the great assembly.

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, knows as it truly is the establishment of the distinctions between the various meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), and meditative absorptions (*samādhi*) of all sentient beings, as well as their defilement, purification, liberation, and complete purity."

If the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, regarding all sentient beings and all their meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), and meditative absorptions (*samādhi*), as well as their defilement, purification, liberation, and complete purity, know them truly by establishing the distinctions between their respective realms, this is called the third power: the knowledge of the powers of meditative concentration, liberation, and meditative absorption.

Possessing this power, he is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; supremely eminent, extraordinary, heroic, and sovereign, he is able to turn the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-wheel and roar the true lion’s roar amidst the great assembly.
"Furthermore, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, knows as they truly are the superior and inferior faculties of all sentient beings.

Because the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha knows as they truly are the superior and inferior faculties of all sentient beings, this is called the fourth power of knowledge regarding the degrees of the faculties."

Possessing this power, he is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; supreme, extraordinary, heroic, and sovereign, he is able to turn the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-wheel and roar the true lion’s roar amidst the great assembly.
"Furthermore, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, knows as they truly are the various inclinations, desires, and diverse dispositions of all sentient beings."

Because the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, know as they truly are the various inclinations, dispositions, and differences in the realms of all sentient beings, this is called the fifth power, the knowledge of the power of the differences in inclinations, dispositions, and realms.

Possessing this power, he is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; supreme, extraordinary, heroic, and sovereign, he is able to turn the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-wheel and roar the true lion’s roar amidst the great assembly.

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, knows as they truly are the various elements, lineages, and distinctions of realms among all sentient beings in all worlds, which are not of a single kind.

If the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, regarding all sentient beings and the entire world, know as they truly are the various and manifold elements, lineages, and distinctions of realms, this is called the sixth power of knowledge: the power of knowing the various elements.

Possessing this power, he is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; he is supremely exalted, extraordinary, and heroic, possessing sovereign mastery to turn the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-wheel, and he rightly roars the lion’s roar amidst the great assembly.
"Furthermore, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, knows as they truly are the paths leading everywhere for all sentient beings.

Because the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha knows as they truly are the paths leading everywhere for all sentient beings, this is called the seventh power of knowledge regarding the paths leading everywhere."

Possessing this power, he is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; most honored, supreme, extraordinary, heroic, and sovereign, he is able to turn the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-wheel and roar the true lion’s roar amidst the great assembly.

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, with respect to the infinite past lives of sentient beings—whether it be one birth up to ten births, or twenty births up to a hundred, a thousand, or immeasurable births; or even one kalpa of increase and decrease, up to hundreds of thousands of immeasurable kalpas of increase and decrease—he knows them all as they truly are."

Regarding the various names of sentient beings, as well as their respective locations, lineages, food and drink, experiences of suffering and pleasure, and the length of their lifespans and duration of stay—knowing truly that when their lifespan is exhausted in one place they are reborn in another, and when their life ends here they are reborn there, including all their formations (*saṃskāra*), consciousnesses (*vijñāna*), and perceptions (*saṃjñā*) in those places of existence—this is called the eighth power of knowledge: the knowledge of past abodes (*pūrvanivāsajñānabala*).

Possessing this power, he is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; he is supremely eminent, extraordinary, heroic, and sovereign, able to turn the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-wheel and to roar the true lion’s roar amidst the great assembly.

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, with the pure divine eye that surpasses that of humans, perceives sentient beings as they die and are reborn; he knows, exactly as it is, their beautiful and ugly forms, their superior and inferior conduct, and how their performance of wholesome and unwholesome deeds results in wholesome and unwholesome retributions."

Furthermore, he sees sentient beings who commit evil deeds of body, speech, and mind, who revile the noble ones and give rise to great false views; having performed such actions of false view and being possessed of these karmic conditions, at the breaking up of the body after death, they fall into the three evil realms.

Furthermore, seeing sentient beings who initiate wholesome physical conduct as well as verbal and mental karma—neither slandering the noble ones nor disparaging right faith, their minds possessing right view and initiating karmic actions of right view—and knowing as it truly is that through these karmic conditions, at the breaking up of the body and the end of life, they will be reborn in the heavens; this is called the ninth power of knowledge regarding death and rebirth.

By virtue of possessing this power, he is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; he is supremely eminent, extraordinary, heroic, and sovereign, capable of turning the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-wheel and uttering the true lion’s roar amidst the great assembly.

"Furthermore, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, regarding the meditative absorption of the exhaustion of all outflows, dwells having realized through direct knowledge and wisdom the liberation of mind and the liberation by wisdom, knowing for himself as it truly is: 'Birth has been exhausted, the holy life has been established, what was to be done has been accomplished, and there is no further existence after this.'"

If the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, regarding the meditative concentration on the exhaustion of outflows, abide in the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom through their own realization of direct knowledge, knowing as it truly is: "Birth has been exhausted, the holy life has been established, what was to be done has been accomplished, and there is no further existence"—this is called the tenth power of knowledge, the power of the exhaustion of outflows.

Possessing this power, he is named Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; supreme, distinguished, heroic, and sovereign, he is able to turn the unsurpassed, pure Brahma-wheel and roar the true lion’s roar amidst the great assembly.

At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished speaking this sutra, the assembly of bhikṣus, as well as the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, and others, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Ten Powers Spoken by the Buddha
